circle_level_observations.text: The interview names several close contacts who could merit social-circle inclusion: Walter (82, chess/bingo partner at the senior center every other Thursday, Q07) and Brian's father (Sunday dinners every week, Q05). Neither is in the five-member circle. The current five (wife, best friend, brother-in-law, mother, sister) is a defensible high-density inner ring, and the five-member cap forces tradeoffs. Walter and the father remain documented in the extracted profile and surface as activity partners; their absence from the circle is acceptable given the cap.
Gender balance: three women (Megan, Linda, Karen), two men (Tony, Mike). Reasonable for Brian's documented network.
Geographic distribution (Pompano Beach, Margate, Tampa, Boca Raton, Jacksonville) reflects the interview-stated family map and is internally coherent.

verification.verdict_rationale: All five social circle members map cleanly to interview-named people with verdicts of consistent. Inferred details (surnames, ages, exact occupations, recent text topics) are flagged as gaps but carry forward as reasonable extrapolation from documented relationships. No INCONSISTENT verdicts, no FLAG_FOR_REVIEW actions, no REPLACE_PERSON/ENRICH/DROP/ADD dispositions required.

social_circle.name: Megan Martin

demographics.occupation: Dental hygienist at a private practice on Sample Road, Pompano Beach
demographics.education: Associate of Science in Dental Hygiene

background.how_they_met: Introduced at Tony's Memorial Day cookout in Coconut Creek in May 2010; she was Tony's cousin's roommate. They bonded over the Red Sox because she grew up outside Boston before her family moved south.
background.why_close: Married twelve years, two children together, co-managing a household rebuilt around Brian's 2023 back injury. Brian describes her as the steady one when he gets spun up about money or work, and the partner who reset the household plan with him on a yellow legal pad after the injury. She is also his primary emotional regulator, the one who flagged his post-injury alcohol uptick and caught him crying in the garage during the February insurance flare.

key_traits: detail-oriented at work, low-drama at home
interests: Roth IRA and long-term household planning
local school board and city races
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Full sentences, punctuation intact, mixes practical logistics with brief affection. Sends pictures of Hannah's art, sends grocery list adds as new texts rather than corrections, occasional heart emoji but rarely more than one. Will switch to a phone call if it's anything emotionally heavy.

shared_activities: Sunday family dinners with Brian's parents (Megan does the roast, Brian does the sides)
Sunday-night household budget review on Brian's spreadsheet
Annual summer trip to her family in Massachusetts
Watching Red Sox games together in the evening after the kids are down
Tag-teaming the Tyler/Hannah pickup and drop-off schedule
recent_text_topics: Logistics around Hannah's noon pre-K pickup and which of them is grabbing Tyler from little league practice on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
The next homeowner's insurance renewal estimate and whether to shop carriers before it comes through again at the previous +40% rate.
Whether Brian should test for the BPI cert in October or push to November — she has been pushing him toward October so he can file the business on schedule by spring.
Coordinating the Massachusetts trip for late July, including whether Mike will fly up to meet them there.
Small daily affection — gym pictures of the kids, 'pick up milk' adds, and a recurring joke about how Tony always shows up empty-handed on game night.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q01: 'Met my wife, Megan, at a friend's barbecue in 2010, married her in 2013.' Q05: 'Megan, she's thirty-seven, works as a dental hygienist over at a practice on Sample Road. We've been married twelve years this October.' Q05 follow-up: 'She's the steady one when I get spun up about money or work.' Q38: 'Megan called me on it, so I've pulled it back.' Q44: 'Megan caught me crying in the garage one night.' Q23: 'Megan's the one who keeps me on top of the local races.'

social_circle.name: Tony Castellano

demographics.occupation: Owner-operator of a small residential roofing crew in Margate (4-5 guys)
demographics.education: High school diploma plus roofing trade experience

background.how_they_met: Mutual friends in the Broward trades scene in the early 2000s; Tony threw the Memorial Day 2010 cookout in Coconut Creek where Brian met Megan.
background.why_close: Brian calls him 'basically a brother.' They run in the same construction-trades world, both are tradesmen-turned-small-business-operators, and they have an explicit pact to not let politics blow up the friendship. Tony was also the matchmaker (accidentally) for Brian and Megan. They see each other at least once a week and talk every couple of days.

key_traits: generous with his crew and his time
all-in or all-out, no middle gear
interests: Dolphins football (loud Dolphins-Patriots rivalry with Brian)
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Short texts, all-lowercase, plenty of typos, voice notes when he is on a roof and can't type. Heavy use of '😂' and the crying-laughing face. Sends memes about contractor life and the occasional unsolicited weather radar screenshot before a storm.

shared_activities: Watching Red Sox games and football together at one of their houses on rotation
Trading handyman job leads (Tony refers small interior work that's beneath his crew, Brian refers roof inspections)
Spring softball at Mitchell Moore Park together
Camaro project consults (Tony brings tools Brian doesn't have)
Cookouts where their kids hang out
recent_text_topics: Tony trying to talk Brian into adding roof-component knowledge to his BPI study so they can cross-refer customers once Brian's business is licensed.
Softball league scheduling for the spring season at Mitchell Moore Park — who is playing shortstop now that one of the regulars moved.
Tony's truck transmission going out and asking Brian if he knows a non-dealer mechanic who won't gouge him.
Sox-vs-Yankees trash talk and Brian needling Tony when the Dolphins lose.
A running thread where Tony keeps sending shingle photos asking 'guess the year' and Brian guesses wrong on purpose.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q01 follow-up: 'Buddy of mine, Tony, threw a Memorial Day cookout in 2010 over in Coconut Creek.' Q07: 'Tony, the guy who threw the barbecue where I met Megan, he's basically a brother to me at this point. He runs a small roofing crew in Margate, we talk every couple days.' Q07 follow-up: 'At least once a week. Either he's at our place watching a game or I'm helping him with something at his.' Q24 follow-up: 'Tony and I disagree on a lot of stuff and we just don't go there.' Q49: 'If I'm having a hard time, I talk to Megan, Tony, or my therapist.'

social_circle.name: Mike Sullivan

demographics.occupation: Marine electronics technician (boat wiring, sonar, GPS installs) at a marina in Tampa

background.how_they_met: Through Megan when Brian started dating her in 2010; Mike was her younger brother, then a teenager. Family bond cemented after the 2013 wedding.
background.why_close: Brian explicitly calls them 'tight.' Fishing is their shared language: Mike has a flats boat and they chase snook and redfish together. Mike is also the only person in Brian's life he openly fantasizes about the Azores sailing trip with.

key_traits: more bohemian than the rest of the family
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Mixes texts with photo dumps from the dock. Sends short captions like 'look at this one' with a snook photo. Uses the fish emoji a lot. Will go silent for 3-4 days when he's on a charter, then resurface with a long catch-up text.

shared_activities: Saltwater fishing trips on Mike's flats boat (snook and redfish)
Planning the aspirational Azores sailing trip
Family gatherings when Mike comes east to Pompano
Talking Tyler through 'when can Uncle Mike take me fishing'
recent_text_topics: Snook season opener and whether Brian can drive over for a Saturday charter once his back gets through the next PT cycle.
Mike sending links to used Catalina 34s and Pearson 36s as 'research' for the Azores trip, with Brian sending back insurance horror stories.
Mike asking about Tyler's birthday and whether a junior fishing rod is too much (Megan says it isn't).
Coordinating whether Mike will drive up to meet the family in Massachusetts this summer or fly direct.
A running joke about Mike calling Brian's Camaro 'a money pit on land' and Brian calling Mike's boat 'a money pit on water.'
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q06: 'Just my brother-in-law Mike, Megan's brother, he lives in Tampa. We're tight, we go fishing whenever I can get over there.' Q06 follow-up: 'Snook mostly, sometimes redfish in the flats. He has a little flats boat.' Q108: 'I'd love to take that sailing trip to the Azores with my brother-in-law.'

interests: her Southern Baptist church in Boca

shared_activities: Sunday family dinner at Brian and Megan's house
Wednesday phone call
Holiday hosting (the parents stay over at Brian's place)
Watching the grandkids when Brian and Megan need a break
Faith-related conversations during Brian's anxiety flare-ups

recent_text_topics: Asking about Brian's back after his February flare and whether he's been doing his PT consistently.
Sharing photos of Brian's dad's cardiology follow-up paperwork and asking Brian to help interpret the chart.
Sunday dinner menu — whether she should bring her potato salad or let Brian handle the sides this week.
Forwarded prayer chain about a neighbor in Boca who lost her husband, with a note 'thinking of you and the kids.'
Coordinating Hannah's 5th-birthday celebration plans for next year and asking what to get Tyler for finishing 2nd grade.

social_circle.name: Karen Martin-Whitlock

demographics.education: Bachelor's in English education, plus state teaching certification

background.how_they_met: Brian's older sister; grew up together in Coral Springs in the same household.
background.why_close: Long-distance but durable: phone calls every couple of weeks and visits about twice a year. shared_activities: Twice-yearly family visits (one usually around the holidays)
Parenting comparison conversations — her three kids vs. Tyler and Hannah
Long phone calls about politics, race, and family
Coordinating care around their parents (especially since their dad's 2022 heart attack)
social_circle.communication_frequency: every couple of days for short texts, longer calls every two weeks
recent_text_topics: Checking in about their dad's last cardiology appointment and whether Linda is being too anxious about his diet.
Sending Brian an article about Florida's home-energy retrofit incentives and asking how the BPI study is going.
A back-and-forth about Tyler being a little behind on reading — she's offered second-grade book lists and reading-aloud tips.
Continuing a conversation from a Q&A on race where she pushed Brian to read a specific book; he hasn't finished it and she keeps gently checking.
Planning the next visit — whether she and her family come down for Thanksgiving or Brian's family drives up to Jacksonville first.
